narration: First, a camera casts rays into the 3D scene, sampling continuous query points along each ray.
Next, each sampled point queries multi-resolution 3D feature grids, interpolating coarse and fine geometric features.
A neural MLP processes the interpolated features to predict signed distance fields for individual scene objects.
A minimum operation aggregates object SDFs into the overall scene SDF, regularized by Eikonal and interpenetration losses.
From the scene SDF, transmittance and ray weight distributions are computed to model continuous light attenuation.
Transmittance modulates object densities into occlusion-aware opacities, which are supervised using 2D instance masks.
Finally, volume rendering synthesizes depth, surface normals guided by pretrained priors, and RGB color under multi-modal losses.
